name: Software Heritage — independent archival of this estate
description: Third-party archival state. Software Heritage has archived this estate on its own initiative; this door records what it holds, with the SWHID, so the durability claim is checkable rather than asserted.
why_this_matters: Every other durability claim in this estate rests on our own signature. This one does not: Software Heritage is an independent, UNESCO-backed archive that crawled and stored these origins without being asked, so the bytes survive us and the archival is not our assertion.

the_30_pkg_go_dev_entries_are_NOT_go_pac.finding: A first read of these counts suggested the estate publishes 30 Go modules that its own registry census (329 PyPI + 1 npm, no Go) had missed. It does not.
the_30_pkg_go_dev_entries_are_NOT_go_pac.result: 404 — and the GitHub repository behind it is Python, not Go.
the_30_pkg_go_dev_entries_are_NOT_go_pac.explanation: pkg.go.dev synthesises a page for any importable-looking path, and Software Heritage archived those pages. The origins are real archive records of URLs; they are not evidence of Go packages.
the_30_pkg_go_dev_entries_are_NOT_go_pac.conclusion: The registry census was correct. This entry exists so the next reader does not rediscover the same false lead and publish it.

what_this_does_not_establish: Software Heritage does not endorse, review or verify the Council of AI. It archives source code, and archival is not approval.

An archived snapshot proves the bytes existed at the visit date. It is not a timestamp anchor for a measurement, and it does not substitute for the missing root anchor recorded at /.well-known/anchor-posture.json.
57 origins is what a keyword search returns; it is not a curated inventory of what the estate considers its own.
doctrine: An independent archive is worth more than our own copy, and worth less than an anchor. Both are stated.
